targetText: Millions upon millions of women in such families live (or, rather, exist) as “domestic slaves”, striving to feed and clothe their family on pennies, at the cost of desperate daily effort and “saving” on everything: except their own labour.
explanation: Lenin characterizes the double burden of working-class women under capitalism: domestic confinement and unremitting daily toil to stretch meager family budgets, which capitalists exploit to drive down general wage levels.

targetText: And no amount of “moral indignation” (hypocritical in 99 cases out of 100) about prostitution can do anything against this trade in female flesh; so long as wage-slavery exists, inevitably prostitution too will exist.
explanation: Lenin sweeps aside bourgeois moralizing, identifying prostitution as an inevitable institutional outcome of capitalist wage exploitation that forces impoverished women to sell their bodies to survive.

targetText:
All the oppressed and exploited classes throughout the history of human societies have always been forced (and it is in this that their exploitation consists) to give up to their oppressors, first, their unpaid labour and, second, their women as concubines for the “masters”.

Slavery, feudalism and capitalism are identical in this respect. It is only the form of exploitation that changes; the exploitation itself remains.
explanation: A sweeping historical materialist generalization: across every antagonistic mode of production, patriarchal exploitation and class subjugation intersect, compelling the exploited to yield both surplus product and sexual access to the ruling class.

targetText: A display of proletarian women’s poverty and indigence will bring a different benefit: it will help wage-slaves, both men and women, to understand their condition, look back over their “life”, ponder the conditions for emancipation from this perpetual yoke of want, poverty, prostitution and every kind of outrage against the have-nots.
explanation: Lenin emphasizes the political importance of working-class agitation and exposure: unveiling the unvarnished realities of female oppression breaks working-class fatalism and builds revolutionary solidarity across sexes.
